lines.li: [us] Is {HEAD} a good {HEADTITLE}?
[them,role:heir] Good enough that I'm in no hurry to take the seat.
[them,their:tribal] {HEAD} listens before speaking, which is all we ask of anyone who leads.
[them] Fair, and hard to fool, which is the most you can ask.
[us] We could use one of those here.
[them,us:speaker] You are the one they chose, aren't you?
[them] Then grow one, it only takes twenty years.
[them] {HEAD} is new to the seat, and everyone is watching to see what changes.
[us] And what has?
[them,their:medieval] New faces at the hall, and the old faces grumbling outside it.
[them] Not much yet, which some find comforting and some don't.
[us] Give it a season.
[them] That's what the old ones say, give it a season.
[us] It must be hard, running {TOWN}.
[them] Everyone wants something, and they all want it by tomorrow.
[us] How do you manage?
[them,their:tribal] I listen, I sleep on it, and then I ask the oldest woman in camp.
[them] I listen to everyone, and then I do what I was going to do anyway.
[us] That sounds like good advice.
[us] You'll lead {TOWN} one day, they say.
[them] One day, and I hope {HEAD} keeps it a long time first.
[us] You're not in a hurry?
[them] I've watched what the seat does to people, so no.
[us] What does an envoy actually do?
[them] Walks a long way, smiles a lot, and remembers everything everyone says.
[us] Everything?
[them] Everything, so mind what you tell me.
[us] Is {LEADER} still {LEADERTITLE} of your people?
[them] Still, and likely to be for a while yet.
[us] Is that good?
[them,their:tribal] The spirits seem content, so we are too.
[them] Good enough, and better than some I could name.
[us] How is {NOTABLE} getting on, your {NOTABLETITLE}?
[them] Busy as ever, and telling everyone so.
[us] Give {NOTABLE} our regards.
[them] I will, and I'll say they came from {COLONIST} of {COLONY}.
[them] I'll be glad to get home, {ILL} is ailing and I'd rather be near.
[us] Is it serious?
[them] Serious enough that people speak quietly around the house.
[us,us:best:Medicine] If it would help, I could tell you what I'd try.
[us] Then I hope you get home quickly.
[them] Thank you, I'll take any kindness going.
[them] {TOWN} feels emptier since we lost {LOST}.
[us] I'm sorry, were you close?
[them,their:tribal] In a camp like ours, nobody is far from anybody.
[them] Close enough, in a town where everyone knows everyone.
[us] Then I'm sorry for all of you.
[them] It always feels sudden, however it comes.
[us] Has the war with {WAR} reached {TOWN}?
[them,war:losing] Closer than I'd like, we've fewer towns than when it began.
[them,war:winning] Not the walls, and it's going the other way now.
[them] Not the walls, but it's in every conversation.
[us] I hope it stays that way.
[them] The young hunters paint their faces now and talk only of {WAR}.
[us] And the old ones?
[them] The old ones remember the last war, so they say nothing at all.
[them] Every smith at home has made spearheads since the war with {WAR} began.
[us] And the plowshares?
[them] They'll wait, the plowshares always wait.
[them] Half the trucks at home are carrying ammunition now, with {WAR} the way they are.
[us] And the other half?
[them] Carrying people away from wherever the ammunition is going.
[us] What's an ordinary day like in {TOWN}?
[them,their:tribal] Up with the light, out to the hunt or the fields, back by the fire at dark.
[them,their:medieval] Bells, bread, work, more bells, and the tavern if there's coin.
[them,their:hightech] Work, eat, argue about the news, sleep, and do it again.
[them] Work, food, gossip and sleep, in roughly that order.
[us] Not so different from here.
[them] No place is, once you've been there a week.
[us] What do people do for fun in {TOWN}?
[them,their:tribal] Dance, wrestle, and tell the same jokes about the neighbors.
[them,their:medieval] Dice, ale, and arguing about whose turn it is to buy.
[them,their:hightech] Cards, music, and whatever's on the radio when it works.
[them] Music, games and gossip, mostly the gossip.
[us] We're the same.
[them] Then you'd fit right in.
[us] What's the food like in {TOWN}?
[them,home:coast] Fish, fish and fish, and bread when the boats come back empty.
[them,home:desert] Flatbread, dates and anything that keeps in the heat.
[them,home:frozen] Dried meat, and a soup that's been on the fire since before I was born.
[them] Plain, filling, and nobody complains where the cook can hear.
[us] I'd eat it gladly, after a day on the road.
[us] Who keeps the peace in {TOWN}?
[them,town:head] {HEAD}, when it comes to it, and everyone's mother the rest of the time.
[them] Everyone's mother, mostly, and the rest of us when we must.
[us] It sounds like it works.
[them] Most days, and the other days we talk about for years.
[us] Is {TOWN} a big place?
[them,their:tribal] Small enough that everyone is someone's cousin.
[them,their:medieval] A mill, a market and far too many geese.
[them,their:hightech] Big enough to get lost in, small enough that someone will find you.
[them] Big enough, and every year a little bigger.
[us] We're working on bigger ourselves.
[them] If you're ever in {TOWN}, ask for the faithful of {THEIRFAITH}, they'll take you in.
[us] I'll remember that.
[them] Do, the road is long and our people are kind to their own.
[them] It's haymaking at home, every back in {TOWN} is bent in the fields.
[us] And you got out of it?
[them,role:trader] Somebody has to sell the hay, don't they?
[them] I'll pay for it when I get back, believe me.
[us] What do the children do all day in {TOWN}?
[them,their:tribal] Follow the hunters, and get sent back, and follow them again.
[them] Get under everyone's feet, and learn more than we teach them.
[us] Ours are the same.
[them] More of ours will be along soon, so I hope you've room.
[us] There's always room for good company.
[them] Then they'll be good company, I'll see to it.
